options.title: Monitor bed availability for CTAS patients
options.description: Establish a process to monitor bed availability for CTAS 1 and 2 patients upon arrival, ensuring immediate access to a monitored bed as per policy.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: If successful, this option could alleviate pressure on the physician lead and charge nurse. However, it may shift the burden to the triage RN, who will need to ensure timely bed allocation.
options.how_we_would_know: Monitor the number of CTAS 1 and 2 patients who receive immediate access to a monitored bed within a defined timeframe.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the intervention leads to a significant increase in bed availability for CTAS patients, it can be considered successful and may not require further action.

options.title: Adjust rooming pace during high occupancy
options.description: Implement a process to adjust rooming pace during periods of high bed occupancy and slow physician pace to ensure a better match between rooming and clinician capacity.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: This option may shift pressure to the triage RN or other staff responsible for managing rooming. It's crucial to ensure that the adjusted rooming pace aligns with the capacity of available physicians.
options.how_we_would_know: Measure the impact on bed availability and wait times for CTAS patients during periods of high occupancy.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the adjusted rooming pace leads to consistent bed availability for CTAS patients, it can be considered successful and may not require further action.

options.title: Communicate expected waits to patients
options.description: Establish a process to communicate expected wait times to patients after rooming, especially during periods of high bed occupancy and slow physician pace, to manage patient expectations and reduce complaints.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: This option may shift pressure to the triage RN or other staff responsible for communicating wait times. It is important to ensure that the communicated wait times are accurate and regularly updated.
options.how_we_would_know: Monitor patient complaints about waiting times and assess whether the new communication process has reduced the number of complaints.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If patient complaints about waiting times decrease significantly, it can be considered successful and may not require further action.

recommendation.rationale: Given the observed pattern, option O1 directly addresses the gap by establishing a process to monitor bed availability for CTAS patients.
recommendation.would_change_if: If further analysis reveals systemic issues affecting physician availability or pace, the recommendation may need revision.

suggested_reviewers.why: To ensure alignment with risk management strategies and patient safety.
To provide context on bed availability and patient flow, and ensure feasibility.
